newsitem.title: CHINA: VW-Audi unworried by China Audi lookalike.
newsitem.headline: VW-Audi unworried by China Audi lookalike.

text.p: German car maker Volkswagen AG said on Thursday it was not worried that an Audi look-alike car made by its Chinese joint venture partner would hurt its position in the rapidly-growing market.

Volkswagen's Chinese joint venture partner First Auto Works, which also had a licencing agreement with the German auto firm's Audi arm, has been producing an Audi-based car marketed under its Red Flag name.

First Auto, based in the northeast China city of Changchun, last month said it would offer two billion yuan of domestic currency A shares in a move analysts said may allow it to try to take on its joint venture partners in the passenger car market.
First Auto has said it would use the funds raised from the share issue to expand now modest production of the Red Flag to 90,000 cars a year by 2000.

"The technology transfer (deal) gave the Chinese the right to develop their own version of the Audi, and that's what they did with the Red Flag," said Eric Carlson, sales manager for Volkswagen Asia-Pacific.
Carlson said Audi, which now produces only a few thousand cars a year in China, was hoping to make its newer, high-end A6 model with First Auto.
Audi officials appeared to want to distance themselves from the Red Flag, saying the Chinese car shared little with its pricey German cousin.
"The Red Flag is a total product of their own," said Audi spokesman Axel Engel. "It bears no Audi nameplates."
Other Audi officials said Audi's sales would not suffer in China because it still offered a high-quality product aimed at a different niche than the Red Flag.
"We know quite well from market research that customers learn to distinguish the cars," said Christina Schlichting, Audi representative in China.
